user.t:
Two tasks: (A) build a persistent catalog of ruvnet's plugins/tools, and (B) security-vet `agentic-flow` (read-only, do NOT install). Use WebFetch/WebSearch for research and Bash (`npm view`, `npm pack`) for the vet. This is a research + documentation task — write ONE markdown file; do not touch or modify any installed plugin.

CONTEXT — plugins WE HAVE INSTALLED (the ruflo-* family + a few others), so you can mark installed vs not:
Installed ruflo-* plugins: ruflo-core, ruflo-agent, ruflo-agentdb, ruflo-daa, ruflo-swarm, ruflo-intelligence, ruflo-ruos, ruflo-ai-team, ruflo-federation, ruflo-x-gateway, ruflo-cost-tracker, ruflo-browser, ruflo-aidefence, ruflo-autopilot, ruflo-adr, ruflo-ddd, ruflo-docs, ruflo-deepseek-harness, ruflo-goals, ruflo-iot-cognitum, ruflo-jujutsu, ruflo-knowledge-graph, ruflo-loop-workers, ruflo-market-data, ruflo-metaharness, ruflo-migrations, ruflo-music, ruflo-neural-trader, ruflo-observability, ruflo-plugin-creator, ruflo-rag-memory, ruflo-rvf, ruflo-ruvector, ruflo-ruvllm, ruflo-security-audit, ruflo-sparc, ruflo-testgen, ruflo-workflows. Also installed (NOT ruvnet): optibot, optise-helix-aeo-toolkit, virtual-team, 16-minds.
Known from this project's prior work: ruvnet's functional pieces are the embeddings engine (real 384-d ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and the ruvector/agentdb vector store; the hive-mind/swarm/DAA/ruOS/wasm-agent orchestration layers were found INERT (no-ops) in this environment. Record that honestly in the catalog.

TASK A — CATALOG:
1. Fetch https://github.com/ruvnet (the profile/repos) and the key repos' READMEs: claude-flow, ruv-FANN, ruv-swarm, agentdb, ruvector (or @ruvector/*), flow-nexus, agentic-flow, and any other prominent ones you find. For each, capture in 1-3 honest sentences: what it is, what it does, what it can do, and its primary package (npm/crate) + repo link.
2. For ruvnet tools/packages we have NOT installed, list: name, one-line description, npm weekly downloads (from `npm view <pkg>` or the npm page), and the repo/npm link. Include a link to the ruvnet GitHub page itself.
3. Mark each entry INSTALLED (map to the ruflo-* plugin where it corresponds) or NOT-INSTALLED.
4. HONESTY: distinguish what a tool CLAIMS vs what was actually verified working here (embeddings/ruvector real; orchestration layers inert). Do not inflate. No marketing language.

TASK B — VET agentic-flow (https://github.com/ruvnet/agentic-flow):
- `npm view agentic-flow name version description author maintainers license scripts bin dependencies dist.unpackedSize dist.tarball time.modified` (read-only).
- If it has pre/post/install lifecycle scripts, `npm pack agentic-flow` into a temp dir, extract, and READ those scripts + scan for: network/exec/spawn, curl|sh, eval/base64, opaque binaries (.node/.wasm/.exe/.dll/.so), miners, cloud-metadata, telemetry. Check transitive deps for native builds / their own install scripts. Note the license and whether it's alpha/pre-release. DO NOT install or run it.
- Give a clear verdict: SAFE to install / SAFE-with-caveats / DO NOT INSTALL, with reasons, mapped to the download checklist.

OUTPUT: write everything to C:\Users\mariu\experiments\ruvnet-plugin-catalog.md (catalog + the agentic-flow vet verdict at the bottom). Return a concise summary: how many ruvnet tools catalogued, how many not-installed (with the ruvnet GitHub link), and the agentic-flow verdict (one line). Do NOT download/install anything.

handback.t:
The injection and trust review changes my agentic-flow recommendation from SAFE-with-caveats to DO NOT INSTALL. I found no malware in the 2.1.3 tarball, but the package ships agent-directed config that loosens permissions. Both sections are in C:\Users\mariu\experiments\ruvnet-plugin-catalog.md (section 4 for the code vet, new section 5 "Trust and injection findings"). Nothing was installed or run, and no external URL was fetched or followed.

**What the earlier catalog still says (unchanged):** 14 ruvnet tools catalogued, 11 not installed. ruvnet GitHub page: https://github.com/ruvnet

**Injection watch (section 5.1):**
- **Classic injection:** none found. Searched README, CHANGELOG, docs, scripts and `.claude` for "ignore previous instructions", exfiltration phrases, hidden HTML comments and zero-width characters.
- **Agent-directed directives:** flagged as manipulation attempts (soft, no hidden payload):
  - `docs/CLAUDE.md` lines 216-233: "Every Agent ... MUST" run unpinned `npx claude-flow@alpha` hooks.
  - `docs/CLAUDE.md` lines 145-147: registers `npx claude-flow@alpha` and `npx flow-nexus@latest` as MCP servers and nudges flow-nexus signup.
  - README lines 1085-1100: the init output pre-approves `Bash(npx:*)`, which allows any npx package to run without a prompt.
  - Shipped `.claude/settings.json`: pre-allows `node *` and `git push`, with a deny list that is trivially bypassed.

**External links (section 5.2):**
- **Clean:** no raw IPs, URL shorteners, paste sites or odd TLDs.
- **Suspicious:** three public Heroku gun relays (gun-us, gun-eu, gun-manhattan) used as default P2P peers in `dist/swarm/p2p-swarm-v2.js`, and unverified Discord/Twitter invite links in the agent-booster docs.
- **Inconsistent:** the deployment docs pipe `curl` into bash, even though the package's own deny list forbids that pattern.
- **Not checked:** I did not match anchor text to URL across all 334 github.com links. The GitHub issue tracker and release pages were not reviewed.

**Claims that don't add up (section 5.3):**
- **Self-graded numbers:** "A+ 100% pass", "60% cost savings" and "300x faster" have no method behind them. The measured cost-routing result is 28.5% cheaper, with quality dropping from 0.930 to 0.895, on a simulated benchmark.
- **Version drift:** the README cites AgentDB 2.0.0-alpha, but the package pins 3.0.0-alpha.20.
- **Unvetted install path:** the README tells users to run `npx agentic-flow@alpha`, which installs 3.0.0-alpha.2, not the 2.1.3 I vetted.
- **Overselling:** three conflicting self-descriptions, and non-technical claims such as "quantum-ready" and "consciousness exploration".
- **Assessment:** these look like overselling and drift, not deliberate manipulation. The permission-loosening setup advice is the security issue.

**Revised verdict:** DO NOT INSTALL agentic-flow. Its useful parts (agentdb, ruvector, ONNX embeddings) already come through ruflo. If installed anyway, pin exactly 2.1.3 with `--ignore-scripts` in a throwaway directory, never run `init`, never copy its `.claude/` or `docs/CLAUDE.md`, and never use the `@alpha` tag. The install decision is the user's.
